extracted.intended_audience: marketers, advertisers, and companies making environmental/"green" product claims
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for marketers on how to craft, qualify, and substantiate environmental ("green") product and marketing claims so they do not mislead consumers. Covers general principles, consumer interpretation, substantiation, and specific topics like certifications, renewable claims, and carbon offsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for environmental marketing claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Green Guides provide general principles that apply to all environmental marketing claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to help marketers avoid making environmental claims that mislead consumers; originally issued in 1992 with revisions in 1996, 1998, and 2012 and updated to be easier for companies to understand and use. Applicable across product types (e.g., recycled paper to biodegradable trash bags).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer interpretation of particular claims
rubrics_metrics.description: How consumers are likely to interpret particular environmental claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketers must consider that what companies think their green claims mean and what consumers really understand can differ; guidance helps predict consumer perceptions to avoid deceptive impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiation of environmental claims
rubrics_metrics.description: How marketers can substantiate particular environmental claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should be backed by appropriate evidence; the Guides explain the kinds of supporting information marketers should have to justify their assertions and avoid deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying claims to avoid deceiving consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: How marketers can qualify their claims to avoid deceiving consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides direction on wording, disclosures, and limitations that marketers can use to clarify claims so consumers are not misled about the scope or benefits of products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of product certifications and seals of approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on marketers’ use of product certifications and seals of approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newer guidance addresses when certifications or seals meaningfully communicate environmental benefits and how their use can be interpreted by consumers; helps marketers avoid implying endorsements or benefits the certification does not support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims about renewable materials and energy sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on claims about materials and energy sources that are described as "renewable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated guidance clarifies how marketers should use the term "renewable" and the substantiation/qualifications needed so consumers are not misled about the renewability of materials or energy sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon offset claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on marketers’ use of "carbon offset" claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guides include direction on how carbon offset claims are likely to be understood by consumers and what substantiation or qualifiers are necessary to avoid deceptive impressions about emissions neutrality or offset effectiveness.
